practice_description.medium: Installation, software, environmental systems, data infrastructure, writing, web-based work
practice_description.practice_summary: Artist and engineer whose practice interrogates environmental data systems, infrastructure governance, and the politics of optimization. She builds alternative environmental management systems that expose how data collection, algorithmic decision-making, and infrastructure design encode specific political and ecological values.
practice_description.methodology: Brain creates functioning technological systems that propose alternative logics for environmental management -- using AI to make deliberately eccentric land-use decisions, building real eccentric water treatment systems, and creating tools that reveal hidden data infrastructure. She combines environmental engineering (background in environmental engineering and interaction design) with art practice, teaching at NYU's ITP program. Her methodology involves building working systems that follow non-optimized logics, revealing by contrast the assumptions embedded in conventional infrastructure. She collaborates with scientists, engineers, and other artists, and has co-authored educational materials on machine learning (co-authored 'AI Art' book with Sam Lavigne).

relevance_to_sense_room.relevance_summary: Brain's practice demonstrates how data infrastructure and environmental systems function as artistic medium. Her work makes visible the governance decisions embedded in data collection and algorithmic management -- directly relevant to how a graph-curated exhibition encodes curatorial values in its infrastructure.
relevance_to_sense_room.art_as_substrate: Partial -- her environmental systems (Asunder, Eccentric Engineering) create infrastructural substrates that produce environmental outcomes. The data pipelines and AI decision systems function as ground layers, but outputs are environmental conditions and policy proposals rather than artworks that others compose with.
relevance_to_sense_room.relational_composition: Yes -- Asunder composes relationships between environmental datasets (satellite imagery, weather data, soil data, water systems) to generate land management proposals. The AI's compositions are determined by relationships between data inputs. Eccentric Engineering creates relational compositions between water treatment systems, plant ecosystems, and environmental sensors.
relevance_to_sense_room.self_recomposing: Yes -- Asunder generates continuously different land management proposals based on changing environmental data inputs. The AI system recomposes its outputs in response to new satellite imagery, weather patterns, and ecological data. Environmental installations like Eccentric Engineering evolve with seasonal and biological changes.

works.title: Asunder
works.description: AI system that generates land management proposals by analyzing satellite imagery, environmental data, and geographical information. The AI makes deliberately non-optimized, eccentric decisions about how to manage landscapes -- proposing flooding cities, rewilding farmland, or redirecting rivers. Presented as a large-scale installation with generated landscape imagery. Created with Julian Oliver and Bengt Sjolen.
works.relevance: Paradigmatic example of AI governance as artistic medium. The system exposes how algorithmic decision-making about environmental resources encodes values. Directly models how an AI curatorial system might make unexpected compositional choices that reveal hidden assumptions.

works.title: Eccentric Engineering
works.description: Series of installations creating alternative water treatment and environmental management systems that follow non-optimized, eccentric logics. Real functioning systems that clean water or manage ecosystems using unconventional approaches (e.g., a fish-controlled water treatment system).
works.relevance: Demonstrates how infrastructure design is a creative act -- the engineering decisions about how a system works encode specific values about efficiency, ecology, and governance. Directly relevant to how A(DAI)'s infrastructure design is itself a creative/political act.

works.title: Smell Dating
works.description: Matchmaking service that pairs people based on body odor rather than algorithmic profiling. Participants wore t-shirts for three days, then smelled samples to choose matches. Created with Sam Lavigne.
works.relevance: Subverts data-driven matching algorithms by using embodied, non-digital information. Exposes how dating platform infrastructure shapes social outcomes -- protocol critique through alternative protocol design.

protocol_art_resonance.protocol_art_summary: Brain treats environmental infrastructure, data systems, and algorithmic governance as artistic medium. Asunder designs an alternative governance protocol for land management; Eccentric Engineering builds alternative infrastructure protocols for water treatment; Smell Dating creates an alternative protocol for social matching. Each work proposes a different set of rules for how systems should operate, exposing the values embedded in conventional infrastructure by contrast.
protocol_art_resonance.system_designed: Asunder: an AI land management governance system that generates eccentric environmental policy proposals. Eccentric Engineering: alternative water treatment and environmental management infrastructure. Smell Dating: an alternative matchmaking protocol based on olfactory rather than algorithmic data. Co-authored educational infrastructure for AI literacy (AI Art book, various syllabi).

commons_orientation.commons_summary: Brain's practice is oriented toward public and commons infrastructure. She teaches at NYU ITP and contributes significantly to open educational resources about AI and environmental systems. Her co-authored book and syllabi are educational commons. Her artworks critique the privatization of environmental data and infrastructure, advocating for public governance of shared resources. The environmental systems she builds propose commons-based alternatives to privatized infrastructure.

governance_model.governance_detail: Asunder deliberately removes human governance from environmental decision-making, handing it to an AI with eccentric logic -- a provocation about who or what should govern shared resources. Eccentric Engineering installations involve biological systems (fish, plants) as governance agents. Brain operates as a solo/collaborative artist but her works raise fundamental questions about algorithmic vs. human vs. ecological governance of infrastructure.

consent_and_authorship.consent_approach: Smell Dating participants explicitly consented to the unusual matching protocol. Environmental installations do not involve personal data. Asunder uses publicly available satellite and environmental data. Brain's practice is generally concerned with collective/environmental consent -- how communities consent (or don't) to the infrastructure and algorithmic systems that govern their environment.
consent_and_authorship.authorship_model: Collaborative -- Asunder was created with Julian Oliver and Bengt Sjolen. Smell Dating with Sam Lavigne. Eccentric Engineering involves biological co-authorship (fish, plants as system agents). Brain typically works in collaboration and credits co-creators, while also maintaining a solo theoretical and educational practice.

liveness_and_duration.temporal_detail: Asunder generates new proposals based on changing environmental data -- the AI system is responsive to satellite imagery updates, weather changes, and ecological shifts. Eccentric Engineering installations are living biological systems that evolve over time with seasonal and biological cycles. Smell Dating was a finite durational project. Works range from responsive-to-input to continuously-evolving depending on the piece.

data_materiality.data_sources: Satellite imagery (Landsat, Copernicus), environmental sensor data (weather, soil, water quality), geographical/topographical data, body odor (Smell Dating), biological sensor data (fish behavior, plant growth), publicly available environmental databases.
data_materiality.data_provenance: Primarily public domain and institutional -- satellite imagery from government programs (NASA, ESA), public environmental databases, and self-generated biological/sensor data. Smell Dating used consented body data. No scraped personal data. Environmental data provenance is a theme of the work.

embedding_space_relevance.embedding_summary: Asunder uses AI/ML models that operate in latent spaces to generate landscape imagery and environmental proposals. The system navigates a learned representation of environmental conditions and land-use patterns. Brain's practice engages with how AI models encode environmental knowledge and what biases are embedded in their training data.
embedding_space_relevance.multimodal: Yes -- spans satellite imagery (visual), environmental sensor data (numerical), geographical data (spatial), biological systems (living organisms), and text/writing. Asunder specifically synthesizes multiple environmental data modalities into visual output.

exhibition_modality.spatial_description: Asunder is presented as a large-scale installation with projected AI-generated landscape imagery and data visualizations in darkened gallery spaces. Eccentric Engineering installations are living systems with water, plants, fish, and sensors -- occupying gallery or outdoor spaces as functioning environmental infrastructure. Works create immersive environments that blur the line between gallery and laboratory/infrastructure.

interoperability.composability: Moderate -- Asunder's outputs (generated landscape proposals, environmental data analyses) could serve as inputs for other systems. Environmental installations produce data streams that could be read by other systems. Educational materials are designed to be used and adapted by others.
interoperability.technical_openness: Partially open. Brain contributes to educational open-source resources. The AI Art book and teaching syllabi are publicly available. Individual artwork code varies in openness.

technical_approach.stack: Python, TensorFlow/PyTorch (for Asunder's AI), satellite imagery processing (GIS tools, Google Earth Engine), environmental sensors (Arduino, Raspberry Pi), web technologies (JavaScript, Node.js), biological systems engineering (aquaponics, constructed wetlands), data visualization libraries.

network_position.scene_affiliation: Environmental/systems art community; NYU ITP (professor); Australian new media art scene (originally); Ars Electronica; Rhizome; critical engineering (Julian Oliver connection); AI art and ethics discourse; SFPC (School for Poetic Computation); environmental humanities.
network_position.connections: Julian Oliver and Bengt Sjolen (Asunder collaborators, Critical Engineering); Sam Lavigne (Smell Dating, AI Art book co-author); Surya Mattu (data infrastructure art); Mimi Onuoha (data politics); connected to NYU ITP network including Dan Shiffman, Allison Parrish; Lauren Lee McCarthy (creative coding/ITP community); environmental art discourse.

potential_role_in_adai.role_detail: Brain's practice offers critical perspective on how data infrastructure encodes values -- essential for A(DAI)'s design of intelligence infrastructure. Her work on environmental governance-as-art parallels A(DAI)'s ambition to build collective intelligence infrastructure where the system design itself is a creative/political act. Her educational focus and experience designing AI systems that reveal their own assumptions could inform how A(DAI) builds transparent, legible infrastructure. Asunder is a direct reference for how AI curation might work in unexpected, non-optimized ways.
